text:
maria: Noticing intermittent interface flaps + elevated RX error counters on g5a instances in us-west-2 (usw2-c). Started ~03:20 UTC, affects intra-node pod-to-pod traffic more than east-west across hosts.

sam: Which counters are spiking? mtu or fragmentation related?

maria: Ran ethtool -S on the affected host (one of the nodes in the canary pool):

maria: ```
ethtool -S eth0 | egrep -i 'rx|tx|checksum|sig|error'
  rx_packets: 1023456
  rx_errors: 245
  rx_bad_checksums: 230
  rx_vhost_signatures_bad: 198
  tx_errors: 0
  tx_dropped: 3
```

alex: dmesg from the same host shows repeated lines like: `ena 0000:00:03.0: Rx signature mismatch (hdr_len=1500, pkt_len=1518)` and `ena: RxBadChecksum`. Might be signature (RSS/GRO/GSO) validation failing after a recent ENA firmware/driver bump.

jia: Are these instances using jumbo MTU (9000)? any path-mtu mismatch with host overlay?

maria: Hosts are set to MTU 9000 cluster-wide. I captured a short tcpdump between two pods on the host and see lots of packets fragmented at 1500 with later checksum corrections that don't match header sig.

maria: ```
# tcpdump -n -vv -s 0 -w - 'host 10.2.5.7 and host 10.2.5.9' | strings | head
14:36:12.123456 IP (tos 0x0, ttl 64, id 54321, length 1518) 10.2.5.7 > 10.2.5.9: Flags [P.], seq 1:1459, ack 1, win 29200, options [nop,nop,TS val 123456 ecr 123450], length 1458
14:36:12.123457 IP (length 1500) 10.2.5.7 > 10.2.5.9: fragment 1/2
... (signatures on NIC disagree with reconstructed packet)
```

sam: This smells like a regression in the ENA driver/firmware combo handling GRO/LRO with jumbo frames. Can you check the driver version?

maria: Driver reported: ena 2.9.1, firmware 1.12.3. We rolled one canary host back to ena 2.8.4 earlier this morning — that host's rx_bad_checksums dropped to single digits and flaps stopped.

alex: Good repro. Short-term mitigation: disable GRO/LRO/GSO on affected hosts. That should reduce the signature glue logic the NIC performs.

jia: Command to flip off offloads: `ethtool -K eth0 gro off lro off gso off tso off` — will increase CPU but avoids NIC-level signature checks. Also consider lowering MTU to 1500 on the host as extra test (will require rolling pods).

maria: I put a one-line runbook in the canary group:

maria: ```
# mitigation steps (canary only)
- ssh canary-host-03
- sudo ethtool -K eth0 gro off gso off tso off
- monitor /var/log/kern.log and `ethtool -S eth0 | egrep 'rx_bad|rx_errors'` for 15m
```

infra-bot: Scheduled: firmware/driver rollback to ena-2.8.4 on canary-host-03 (initiated by maria) — ETA 5m. :wrench:

sam: If rollback looks good on canaries for 1 hour, we should schedule a phased rollback across the cluster with a small batch size (5 hosts) and health checks. Also open ticket with ENA vendor including dmesg, ethtool -S, tcpdump and exact MTU settings.

maria: Filing vendor ticket now and posting logs + pcap link in the ticket. I'll update here after the canary finishes. For now, don't touch MTU cluster-wide; we'll prefer driver rollback + offload flip as temporary controls. :+1:

alex: Also adding a metric alert: host_rx_bad_checksums_rate > 50/min over 3m triggers automations to run the mitigation script on canaries.

maria: Canary rollback succeeded, rx_bad_checksums now 4, no flaps in 22m. Moving to scheduled phased rollback. Will paste rollout plan shortly.

sam: thanks — keep the channel updated and include the rollback playbook in the incident doc.
